title: Labeled exact-degree estimator output
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. For each set of coordinates of size at most $k$, supply the prescribed number of labeled examples, each consisting of a point of the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube and a sign. The output is a sparse Fourier hypothesis supported on those coordinate sets, with each coefficient obtained by rounding the empirical Fourier coefficient computed from the supplied examples to the degree-$k$ Fourier granularity.
hypotheses_covered: for each low-degree coordinate set, a supplied sequence of labeled cube examples of the prescribed length
